summary: The payoff screen: the in-memory model every other vault screen reads, the current total under two pricing modes, per-account balances, the dimension breakdown, and a stacked trend chart drawn in SVG from two independently interpolated series, with a value axis whose ticks are exact and a one-day history drawn whole.

read.role: the price series this view pairs every quantity with

sections: The holding's own list of values
read.role: one holding's figures and as-of dates, drawn from the same model

dataFlow.value: on unlock, fetch all four record types with GET /api/records?type=account|snapshot|rate|profile and decrypt them with the session DEK, then build the model in memory: profile, accounts, snapshots grouped by account_id and sorted by date, and prices grouped by symbol and sorted by date. Subsequent writes update this model directly with no refetch

replacedSinceLastOpenNotice.value: shown when the vault was replaced while the page was locked, or while it stayed open after its session ended for its own reason, and the page learns it only at unlock. A Callout at the top of the content region, above the hero, at the full content width and 32px above it like every other region, a polite live region with no control. It carries the critical icon when kept input was dropped and no icon when none was. It stays until the person leaves the dashboard and is not shown again. A page that learned of the restore before unlocking shows it on the unlock card instead and the dashboard shows none. Unlocking after it lands on the dashboard rather than the view the page was on

theOneRefetch.value: the reload before the first record a sitting creates at a date, which a stale model cannot substitute for

totalFormula.value: total = the sum over active accounts of (latest snapshot.value x price)

pricingModes.value: Latest rates, the default, uses the latest entry for that account's unit whatever date it carries. Rates as of each figure uses the latest entry for that unit at or before the date of the account's own latest snapshot, for every symbol, published ones included, rather than reading not priced where that date has no entry, because every holding in the total must carry a figure for the total to add up. Both modes use the same quantity, and switching makes no network request

pricingModeScope.value: the mode reaches the total, the account list and the breakdown, and nothing else. It is not a chart control and switching it moves no pixel

latestMeansGreatestDate.value: in either series, never the most recently written

mainCurrencyAccounts.value: an account whose unit is the main currency prices at exactly 1 in both modes, from no entry, and is never reported as unpriced

asOfDates.value: each account's figure carries its quantity's as-of date wherever it appears. A row whose price is older than the date it is shown for also carries its price's date, so no figure passes an older price off as the screen's. On latest rates that is a price entry dated before the screen's rate date, the newest date of any entry in the vault. On rates as of each figure it is a price entry dated before the row's quantity date. A row whose price entry sits at that date carries no price date

priceDateLine.value: 'priced 15 Jan 2024', directly beneath a converted figure valued at a price from a day earlier than the one the figure is shown for. Label/meta type in ink-secondary, tabular figures, aligned with the figure, in the figure's own cell or slot and never a column, with the year always shown and the date following Settings. It never takes a status color or an icon. It is absent where the price is from the figure's own day, on a main-currency figure, and on a figure reading 'not priced'. Which day is the figure's own: the dashboard's rate position (Latest rates: the rate date in the control's label; Rates as of each figure: the row's As of date), the recording's date, or a row's date

ratesControlLabels.value: 'Latest rates, 31 July' carries the one rate date for the whole vault. 'Rates as of each figure' carries no date, because the rate date there is the row's own as-of date or the date a row carries where its price is older. The control changes the total, the holdings table and the breakdown and leaves the chart untouched

noStalenessThreshold.value: there is no staleness threshold and no stale-account warning, at any age

exclusions.value: archived accounts are excluded from the current total and remain in history before their archivedAt date. An active account with no snapshots contributes nothing and is listed separately as not yet valued, never as 0. An active account with a quantity and no price for its unit contributes nothing and is listed separately as not priced, never counted at its bare quantity

archivedComesFirst.value: an archived holding is never listed as not yet valued or not priced, because being archived is the stated reason it is out of the total. The two groups list active holdings only. With Show archived on it is an archived row of the holdings table whatever its figures: Archived chip, text in ink-secondary and never reduced opacity, row action Unarchive in place of Record a value. Its unit has no price in the selected mode: Latest value is its latest quantity and In main currency reads 'not priced' with no price date line. It has no readable snapshot: Latest value reads 'not yet valued' and In main currency and As of are empty. With the toggle off it appears nowhere on the dashboard. This holds in both pricing modes. At phone width the right side reads its quantity then 'not priced', or 'not yet valued' with no as-of date. With holdings but no snapshots, active holdings sit under Not yet valued and each archived one is an archived row reading 'not yet valued'

signedSum.value: negative balances subtract, and the UI shows gross assets, gross liabilities and the net figure separately

interpolation.value: value(account, t) = quantity(account, t) x price(unit(account), t). Quantity is linearly interpolated between that account's own snapshots, contributes nothing before its first snapshot and is carried forward after its last. Price is linearly interpolated between that symbol's own entries, carried forward after the last and carried backward before the first. The asymmetry is deliberate

interpolatePerAccountThenSum.value: interpolation is per account and then summed, never interpolation of an already-summed series

samplingRule.value: sample each account at the union of its own snapshot dates and its symbol's price dates within range, plus the range endpoints. Between two samples the segment is drawn straight. Sampling only the snapshot dates would cut every bend off

boundedStretch.value: adding, changing or deleting an entry affects the dates between that entry's neighbors in its own series and no others. The last entry of a series affects everything from the previous entry onward. The first entry of a price series affects everything up to the next entry. An account's first snapshot instead moves where that account's band starts

entryMarks.value: ticks under the x-axis at every date carrying at least one snapshot, on from the moment the chart loads with no stored preference consulted. A tick means a quantity, never a price. A date carrying rate entries and no snapshots bends the bands and takes no tick. Just the line on the dashboard removes them

grouping.value: bands come from a dimension, each account falling in exactly one band per dimension by the record shape rather than by a check. Accounts with no entry, or with an entry naming an archived or unknown value, group under Unassigned, a real band that is never hidden. Grouping by no dimension gives a single band. Band order is fixed per dimension from the configured value order, never sorted by size

coverageIndicator.value: the UI must show how many accounts are assigned wherever a dimension is chosen, because a dimension covering few accounts produces a mostly-Unassigned chart that is correct and useless

valuesBeyondFour.value: the first four in the dimension's configured order take chart slots and the remainder fold into Other

assetsAndLiabilities.value: asset bands stack upward from zero and liability bands mirror downward, each band keeping its group's color on both sides, with the net-worth line over the top

archivedAccountsOnTheChart.value: an account archived on D counts on every chart date before D and on none from D on, so its value at D is part of no total and the chart at D agrees with the current total. Archiving writes the account's zero at D, so the band interpolates into zero like it does between any two snapshots. The zero is the account's new last snapshot, and the archive's refresh may add price entries at D. Each moves exactly what a new last entry moves, the dates after the previous entry in its own series and nothing before it, so every chart point up to and including the latest entry before D of each series the archive wrote to is unchanged. Every archive date carries an annotation on the x-axis and a tooltip line naming the account, with or without a zero

archiveIsAStep.value: a day where a band starts or ends is drawn as a vertical edge at that day's x, from the band's value just before the day to its value at it. The first day of the range has no side before it. An account's first snapshot is absent just before its date and present at it. An account archived on D is present just before D, at D's quantity and D's price, and absent at D. With the zero at D that side is zero, so the step is no edge at all

archivedWithoutAZero.value: an account archived on D whose figure at D is not zero, or which has none, keeps a real step. It falls from D's figure, or from the last quantity carried forward when D has none, with nothing recorded to explain the drop, and D still carries the annotation. Loading such an account writes nothing

archiveDatePriceEffect.value: D's price values the side just before the step, so a price entry at D moves an account archived on D only where that side is non-zero. Only then does the confirmation for a rate change on D count it. With the zero at D, changing the price at D leaves the account's contribution at D and just before D at zero and the confirmation does not count it

unarchivedZero.value: an unarchived account whose zero sits at D contributes zero from D until its next snapshot and interpolates up to that snapshot

valueAtADateIsTheSideAtIt.value: the tooltip, the data table, the hero under the crosshair and the change over a range all read the side at the date. The side just before shapes the drawing only

chartLastDay.value: the newest date carrying a snapshot, a price entry or an archivedAt, and every range counts back from it. An archive whose D carries no snapshot still falls inside the chart

latestRatesRightEdge.value: on latest rates the chart's right hand edge is the total: each active account's last quantity carried forward at its symbol's last price carried forward, with no archived account because it lies at or after every archive. On rates as of each figure the total is deliberately not the edge

firstValuedAndArchivedSameDate.value: appears on no chart date and on neither side of its step: absent just before its first snapshot and absent at its archive

rangesAndToggles.value: ranges 1M, 6M, 1Y and All, defaulting to 1Y or All if history is shorter. An absolute and percentage toggle, where the percentage view normalizes each side against itself, asset bands against total assets and liability bands against total liabilities

nativeQuantityFigures.value: a holding's value in its own unit, in the dashboard's Latest value column and the holding page's Value column, shows as design-system.md Typography, Figures sets it: money at moneyPlaces for a currency unit, and any other unit exactly the decimals stored, never rounded and never padded. The converted figure is money in the main currency

readableDays.value: every calendar day from the range's first day to its last is a date the chart reads. The crosshair, its tooltip, the hero under the crosshair, both ends of a selection and the keyboard each resolve to one such day and read it through the value model, on the side at it. None reads the drawing's samples or its downsampled points. The figure shown is the model's, not the line's

daySpacing.value: for a range of days 0 to n with n at least 1, day k sits at x0 + k * (x1 - x0) / n across the plot, from its left edge x0 to its right edge x1

oneDayRange.value: a range of one day draws its point at (x0 + x1) / 2, whole, at every width, and reads that day at every x. Under 1M, 6M, 1Y and All alike the point's centre sits within half a pixel of the plot's horizontal middle and its mark's bounding box lies wholly inside the chart's drawing, at a 1280px and a 390px viewport

rangeStart.value: a range starts no earlier than the oldest date carrying a snapshot. It counts back from the chart's last day and stops there, so a range longer than the history shows all of it and a history of one day is that one day under every range. A price entry older than the oldest snapshot does not move the start: with snapshots only at 2026-03-01 and 2026-04-10 and a price entry at 2026-01-15, 6M, 1Y and All each start at 2026-03-01

edgeMarksWhole.value: a mark at either edge of the plot is drawn whole at every width: the net-worth line's dot, an entry mark, an archive marker. The plot keeps half the widest mark clear inside its left and right edges

valueTickDomain.value: the value axis carries a gridline and a label at each tick. The domain runs from the lowest drawn value to the highest, zero always included. A domain with no extent, every value zero, runs from 0 to 1

valueTickStep.value: the step is 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten and never below 1: the smallest such number at least the domain's span divided by the target count. Target count: six at desktop width, three at phone width

valueTickPositions.value: ticks sit at i x step for every integer i with i x step inside the domain, computed as that product and never by repeated addition, so every tick is an exact integer. Zero is always a tick

valueTickLabel.value: below a thousand a tick reads as its exact whole number. From a thousand up it reads its magnitude divided by the largest of a thousand, a million and a billion that does not exceed it, with at most one decimal and no trailing zero, then that unit's suffix. Grouped, pointed and signed as money is, so a tick at 1500 reads 1.5 or 1,5 before its suffix by the configured decimal point. No two ticks read the same and a label never rounds its tick, because the domain contains zero, so the step is at least a sixth of the largest tick and a multiple of a 1, 2 or 5 step that large is exact in one decimal of the tick's unit

valueTickPercentage.value: the percentage view takes the same step rule and reads each tick as a whole percent, exact because every tick is an integer

valueTickOnlyAbbreviation.value: a chart's value tick is the one figure that abbreviates. The tooltip, the legend and every other figure show in full, because a tick only places a line and the readout is where a value is read

valueTickLabelPlacement.value: unresolved at desktop width. At phone width the ticks sit in a gutter at the plot's left, outside it, so no tick lies over a band or a mark

pointerRounding.value: k = round((x - x0) * n / (x1 - x0)), clamped to the range, a half rounding to the later day. Every x on the plot reads exactly one day. The pointer at either edge of the plot and at its middle reads that day on a one-day range. Where the plot has at least as many pixels as the range has days, every day is read at some x

selectionEnds.value: the days under the press and the release by the pointer rule, ordered earlier first whichever way the drag ran. The change is the later day's value minus the earlier day's, for the total and for every band. A press and release on the same day is a click

dayArithmetic.value: on calendar dates, never timestamps. A day is a YYYY-MM-DD and the next day is that date plus one, so a daylight-saving change or the reader's time zone cannot skip or repeat a day

chartKeys.value: the chart is focusable and focus puts the crosshair on the range's last day. Left / Right step one day back or forward. Shift+Left / Shift+Right jump to the previous or next marked date, whether or not Just the line has hidden the marks. Home / End jump to the range's first or last day. Enter on a marked date opens its recording and on any other day does nothing. No key moves the crosshair past either end of the range, and a jump with no marked date in its direction leaves it where it is. Focus leaving the chart takes the crosshair away. Each move announces the tooltip's readout and the hero follows

markedDateMeansSnapshot.value: a marked date is a date carrying at least one snapshot, the dates the entry marks sit on. A click or Enter there opens that date's recording, as does the tick under the axis, a click target of its own. On any other day a click or Enter opens nothing

arithmetic.value: all money arithmetic uses the scale-12 BigInt decimal from record-snapshot.md, never floats. Sums are computed at full precision and rounded only for display. A chart point costs two multiplications, both rounding half-even at scale 12

noChartingLibrary.value: the chart is drawn directly in SVG with no charting library, and SVG rather than canvas because the direct labels, tabular-nums figures and the accessible fallback need real DOM. Any library added later must be self-hosted with SRI, CSP-safe with no eval or new Function, and text-only in labels and tooltips. ECharts, ApexCharts and frappe-charts fail structurally because their label and tooltip paths end in innerHTML

accessibility.value: the chart is keyboard reachable (Reading a date) and has a data-table fallback, and each key's readout is the tooltip's text exposed to assistive technology, so a day the table does not list is readable without the pointer. A static aria-label on the SVG is not sufficient for the primary screen of the app

renderingRule.value: every decrypted string is rendered with x-text or textContent, never x-html and never through a chart library that takes an HTML string for labels or tooltips

unreadableRecords.value: a record that fails to decrypt is skipped, the rest of the view renders, and a prominent warning names how many records could not be read. An unreadable price entry drops out of its series and the neighbors interpolate across it. Never swallowed silently and never allowed to crash the view

largeHistory.value: the chart downsamples for display, and totals are always computed on the full data

fixtures: three accounts in different units with known snapshots and known price entries, hand-computed totals in both pricing modes, and the two modes deliberately differing
an account last recorded in March with a price entry from this week, which is the regression fixture for the whole quantity and price split
an account with snapshots of 100 on 1 January and 200 on 1 March, once in the main currency and once in a unit priced 1.00 on 1 January and 2.00 on 1 March, for the straight-line and the bend cases
a date carrying rate entries and no snapshots, kept and removed, for the assertion that it still bends the bands and takes no tick
two accounts whose histories start years apart, for the interpolate-then-sum assertion
two differing entries planted for one (symbol, date), and a second case where that pair is the symbol's only entry
one record deliberately corrupted, once as an account and once as a price entry, for the warning count and the series fallback
a main-currency account with a snapshot of 100 on 1 January 2026 and its zero on 31 January 2026, for the run-down to 50 on 16 January and the absence of a vertical edge at the archive

an account archived on the newest recorded date, and one archived on a date after the newest recording, each with its zero at D, for the right hand edge equal to the total on latest rates and the chart extended to the archive date
an account archived on D with no snapshot at D and one archived with a non-zero snapshot at D, both loaded from a fixture, for the real step, the annotation and the nothing-written-on-load assertion
an unarchived account whose zero sits at D followed by a later snapshot, for the zero until the next snapshot and the interpolation up to it

an XAU-ozt holding stored as "12.125" and an m² holding stored as "80", under moneyPlaces 0 and under 2, for the native-unit column on the dashboard and on the holding page (the formatter criteria are spec/features/account-settings.md#acceptance-criteria)

an account archived on D in a unit that is the only one priced at D, with a price entry at D, once with its zero at D and once loaded with a non-zero snapshot at D, for the side-before-D and the confirmation-count assertions
an account first valued and archived on the same date, for the no-side-present assertion
recordings on 15 January, 10 April and 30 June 2026 and nothing between, for the pointer at the x of 5 February and 3 June, the drag from 3 June back to 5 February, and the day-by-day keyboard walk
a reader time zone with a daylight-saving change inside the range, for the day-stepping assertion
a history long enough to downsample, with a day whose sample the downsampling dropped, for the readout-equals-model assertion
a USD holding whose latest quantity is at 2026-04-10, with USD entries at 2010-03-31 only, for the rates-as-of-each-figure total at the 2010-03-31 rate and the price date it carries
a vault whose newest entry is at 2026-04-10, holding a free-text holding priced only at 2024-01-15 and a USD holding priced at 2026-04-10, for the price date on latest rates

single-holding totals swept from 0.40 to 10^10, covering each 1, 2, 2.5, 5 and 7.5 times a power of ten and the integers either side, positive and negative, rendered at a 1280px and a 390px viewport, for the value tick sweep

one holding recorded at 2500 in the main currency, at a 1280px viewport, under a period and under a comma decimal point, for the ticks 0, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500 and the labels 1.5 and 2.5, then 1,5 and 2,5
a vault with a single recording, at a 1280px and a 390px viewport, under 1M, 6M, 1Y and All, for the point at the plot's middle and wholly inside the drawing
snapshots only at 2026-03-01 and 2026-04-10 and a price entry at 2026-01-15, for the range start

an archived holding in a unit with no price and an archived holding with no readable snapshot, beside an active holding in the first one's unit, in both pricing modes with Show archived on and off, for the archived-row assertions
focus: switching the pricing mode must be asserted over every sample of every band, not only the right hand edge. The mode is defined as changing nothing on the chart, and a test that checks one point passes against an implementation that reprices the whole series

on latest rates the chart's right hand edge must equal the total exactly in decimal, and on rates as of each figure it must deliberately not, with nothing on screen reporting the difference as a fault. Both halves have to be asserted or the mode collapses into a rounding check

the bounded-stretch rule needs all three operations asserted, add, change and delete, with every point outside the stretch compared. A test that only checks the edited date moved says nothing about what else did
the band-sum criterion must hold for every date in the chart in decimal, not at a sampled few. A float path passes a spot check and fails the invariant

the bend assertion must use a price that changes between two snapshots, checking 150 x 1.50 rather than the chord between 100 and 400. An implementation that samples only snapshot dates produces the chord and passes every other chart test
the entry marks must be shown to load on with nothing turned on and no stored preference consulted, and adding a price entry must add no tick. Both are about something not happening

the not-priced state must be shown to exclude the holding from the total and to never count its bare quantity, which is the silent failure: counting a quantity as though its unit were the main currency produces a plausible total

the decryption warning has to be asserted with a real corrupted record, once as an ordinary record and once as a price entry, and the view must still render the rest. Swallowing the failure is the easy path and it is invisible from a screenshot

the archive step needs both sides asserted. With the zero at D the side just before D is zero and no vertical edge is drawn, and the value at D leaves the account out. On an account loaded without a zero the side just before D carries D's quantity and D's price, and the tooltip, data table, hero and change over the range read the value at D. A test of the value at D alone passes an implementation that drops the account one day early

archiving moves nothing up to and including the latest entry before D of each series it wrote to, the account's snapshots and each unit it priced at D, compared point by point before and after. A test that checks only D passes an implementation that redraws the history

the price at D must be asserted to move nothing for an account archived with its zero, with the confirmation not counting it, and to move the side just before the step for one loaded with a non-zero figure at D, with the confirmation counting it. Either half alone passes an implementation that always counts or never counts

the archive-on-newest-date criteria must compare the chart's last point, the data table's last row and the end of the change over the range to the total exactly in decimal, and the archive-after-newest-date case must show the chart extended to the archive date through its zero

the native-unit column must be asserted on both screens that carry it with "12.125" and "80", whose display rounding or padding would change. The converted column, which is money, must still follow moneyPlaces on the same rows

the readout at a day must be asserted against the value model in decimal on days that are not drawing samples, and on a day the downsampling dropped. A readout taken from the nearest drawn point passes at every sample and every recorded date

the pointer walk must run one pixel column at a time across the plot, asserting the day never goes backward, starts at the range's first day and ends at its last, and on a range with no more days than columns reads every day. A few spot positions pass an implementation with a wrong rounding at the half or a clamp missing at an end

the drag must be asserted in both directions, with the selection ordered earlier first and the hero and every legend delta equal to the later day's value minus the earlier day's. A drag left to right alone passes an implementation that does not order the ends

the keyboard walk must be asserted across a daylight-saving change, one day per key press, every day once and in order, with the pointer's readout on each. Day arithmetic done on timestamps skips or repeats a day only there. The recorded-date key must land on every date carrying a snapshot and on no other

a click or Enter on a day carrying no snapshot must open nothing, and on a snapshot day and on its tick must open that date's recording. Asserting only the opening passes an implementation that opens a recording on every click

the no-network criterion must cover the range, the dimension, the absolute and percentage toggle, the pricing mode and band visibility together, captured as requests rather than inferred from the absence of a loading state

the price date must be asserted in both pricing positions with the reference moving: on latest rates a row carries it when its price is dated before the rate date, and on rates as of each figure when its price is dated before the row's own quantity date. A test against the vault's newest entry alone passes an implementation that uses that reference in both positions, and then shows no date on a row whose price is older than its own figure
the price date line must be absent on a row priced at its own day, on a main-currency row and on a not-priced row, and present as a line in the figure's cell, never as a column

the value tick sweep must read every label back through its unit and compare it to its gridline's value exactly, at both viewports and for both signs, with zero a tick and the step never below 1. A few round totals pass an implementation that rounds a label, and a duplicate label shows only across the sweep

the tick at 1500 must read 1.5 under a period and 1,5 under a comma, each before the suffix, and every tick must be an exact multiple of the step. Repeated addition of a step drifts only on some domains
the one-day point must be asserted at both viewports and under all four ranges, on the mark's bounding box and not only its centre. A point at x0 has its centre at an edge and its mark cut in half

the range start must be asserted with a price entry older than the oldest snapshot, because an implementation that counts the range back from the last day to the oldest entry of either series draws an empty stretch ending in a jump

an archived holding must be asserted never to appear under Not priced or Not yet valued, in both pricing modes and at both viewports, as an archived row with the Archived chip, Unarchive and ink-secondary text, while the active holding in the same unit stays under Not priced and with the toggle off the archived holding appears nowhere. A test of the groups alone passes an implementation that drops the archived row, and a test of the row alone passes one that also lists it in a group

the empty state with holdings but no snapshots must be asserted with an archived holding present: active holdings under Not yet valued, the archived one an archived row reading 'not yet valued' only with Show archived on

openQuestions: Selecting a span by dragging has no stated answer on a phone and none from the keyboard. spec/product/net-worth-view.md says it 'needs an answer of its own' and points at spec/product/app-shell.md, which states only the general phone rule. spec/ui/dashboard.md describes Drag in Interaction and its At phone width section is silent on it. Its Keyboard keys (Left / Right, Shift+Left / Shift+Right, Home / End, Enter) only move the crosshair, and none starts, extends or clears a selection, while spec/features/net-worth-view.md, Reading a date, defines a selection only by a press and a release. spec/ui/design-system.md, Accessibility, requires every drag to have a keyboard and pointer equivalent. How a span is chosen by touch and by keyboard is unresolved.

spec/ui/dashboard.md says a plain click clears a selection and that a click with the crosshair on a marked date opens that date's recording. spec/features/net-worth-view.md, Reading a date, calls a press and release on one day a click and says a click on a snapshot day opens its recording. Whether that click also clears a standing selection is not stated.

The suffix of a value tick is stated only by the example "2.5k" in spec/ui/design-system.md, Typography, Figures. spec/features/net-worth-view.md, Value ticks, says each tick reads "that unit's suffix" for a thousand, a million and a billion and names none of them, and the case or locale of the million and billion suffix is not stated. Whether they are M and B, and whether a suffix follows the locale, is unresolved.

Where the value tick labels sit at desktop width is unresolved. spec/features/net-worth-view.md, Value ticks, leaves it to spec/ui/dashboard.md, which says only that the plot spans the card with its value ticks at the left and states the gutter outside the plot at phone width. Whether a desktop tick may lie over a band or an entry mark is not stated.

The target tick count is six at desktop width and three at phone width, and no spec file states the viewport width at which one becomes the other. The same gap is recorded in spec/.compiled/app-shell.json as phoneWidthThreshold, and the 390px and 1280px viewports in the criteria are test widths, not the threshold.

The rate date is stated two ways. spec/features/net-worth-view.md (Current net worth) says it is the newest date of any entry in the vault. spec/ui/dashboard.md (Hero figure, Which rates) and spec/product/net-worth-view.md (The total) say it is the day something was last recorded. The two differ when the last sitting was a backfill at a past date, or when the newest entry is one a person typed. Which date the Latest rates label carries and which date a row's price is compared against is unresolved.

spec/ui/account-detail.md, Header, states the price's date beside the converted figure at the latest price for the holding's unit, and spec/ui/design-system.md, Components, Price date line, leaves which day counts as the figure's own to each screen. The header does not say which day that is, and the dashboard's rates control does not reach it. Which price the header's price date is compared against is unresolved.
